searchText: Thanks. If I understand correctly, you said that limit was added in 2016, does that mean that there might be contracts that are bigger? Do we know what is the biggest contract at the moment? Perhaps not quite the same thing, but the largest input recorded with the valid creation of a contract looks like \xf366261dd4879323763ade1fa0c7fb02a96d6edb9c45b256d9073eeb29d5fba3 although it may be that the tx created multiple contracts so perhaps not what you're after. I'm really looking into the size of the contracts (the bytecode) But that's really interesting. That must be one of the biggest transactions (in bytes and in gas used) You're after the size of the initcode, but not sure anything retains that information explicitly as it requires picking apart the raw transaction data. Biggest tx in terms of gas usage: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x224b0660ab21995e691248d8179f1506f142437d5e6c37537613ac8052fe2138 I might be mistaken about terminology, but I care about max size of the code that is stored in the state, and I don't think that's the initcode. Or am I wrong? Yeah, sorry I don't have the on-chain bytecode sizes, only initcode (which is the data in the tx that creates the contract). max size chosen was a function of how big a contract could be created under the 2016 gas limits. So I doubt a larger contract exists. You would need to inspect on-chain data
